Prompt: A stranger takes your hands. "Your thirst is mine, my water is yours."
Result 1: You give them a dram of fresh water (lose 1 Health). You are water-bonded: the next shop is cheaper.
Result 2: You tell them something you know, and they tell you something back (lose a random Scroll, gain a random Card).
Result 3: Spend 3 Gold: they follow you for your next game.
What it is there: Qud's social ritual: share water with a creature, then trade reputation for secrets, gifts or a follower.
Why it fits: Qud's central social act. The ritual's own menu (share water, give or take a secret, recruit the creature, end it) is already a set of choices with costs. One a run, it is the beat between games that events here are for.

Prompt: The Librarian of the Stilt looks up from her shelves. "Have you brought me something to read?"
Result 1: She shelves it and teaches you what she learned from the last one (Gain +1 Max Health).
Result 2: Nothing.
What it is there: The Librarian of the Six Day Stilt, who takes books in exchange for experience.
Why it fits: At the Six Day Stilt, Sheba Hagadias takes any book you bring her in exchange for experience. Scrolls are this game's books, and turning loot you can't use into something permanent is a choice worth having between games.

Prompt: You come to Delphi. Among the fountains and the centaur statues, the Oracle waits to share her wisdom, for a price.
Result 1: Pay 1 Gold. She tells you a true rumour: see the goals of every game you can reach next.
Result 2: Pay 3 Gold. She speaks at length: Gain +1 Level (the first time only).
Result 3: Her magic missiles answer every blow: lose 2 Health, and she won't speak to you again this run.
What it is there: A unique peaceful NPC on her own level who sells minor (50 gold) and major (500+ gold) consultations; the first of each also gives experience. Attacking her triggers her passive magic missile.
Why it fits: A paid choice between a cheap hint and an expensive reward, which is what events here are. Its prices and outcomes are the wiki's, scaled down.
Needs: new: revealing the next offering's goals

Prompt: Here lie the remains of an adventurer who died where you stand. Their belongings are scattered around them, and something still watches over them.
Result 1: Gain 2 random loot, all unidentified and likely cursed. Their Ghost stands up on the board.
Result 2: Nothing.
What it is there: When a hero dies, the level can be saved and later loaded into another player's game, with their ghost, their killer and their (mostly cursed) belongings.
Why it fits: NetHack's most famous system, and a natural event: loot at a price, and the price stands on the board. Rarity is Uncommon, as real bones levels are.

Prompt: A quiet temple lined with altars, each to a different god. Kneel at one, and its god will ask something of you in return.
Result 1: The god of rage: Gain +2 Strength, but for 3 games you must not use magic.
Result 2: The god of battle: Gain +2 Shields, but for 3 games you must not run from a fight.
Result 3: The god of gold: Gain +4 Gold. Your shops cost 1 more for 3 games.
Result 4: The god of chaos: something random happens, good or bad.
Result 5: You keep your faith to yourself.
What it is there: An optional early branch with altars to many gods; standing on an altar describes the god, and praying there converts you. Each god grants powers and imposes its own conduct.
Why it fits: Choosing a god is Crawl's defining choice, and each god is a boon with a rule attached. That is exactly add_goal's shape (a goal for N games, then the payout). Xom keeps the gamble.

Prompt: Pepin the healer stops you in the square. "The water from the wells has turned foul. Something below is poisoning it. Please, cleanse the source."
Result 1: Add the goal 'Clear an area of every enemy in it' for 2 games. If you do, Pepin gives you a Rare ring.
Result 2: Nothing.
What it is there: A quest from Pepin: the town's water is poisoned by monsters nesting in a cave below level 2; clearing them rewards the Ring of Truth.
Why it fits: A quest-giver's ask is exactly what add_goal events are (Battleworn Dummy is the model): a goal for a few games, then a reward.

Prompt: A knight in rotting armour kneels before you. "Please, don't kill me. I was cursed by my king. Only the Golden Elixir can free me."
Result 1: Add the goal 'Find a potion or elixir' for 3 games. If you do, he gives you his helm before he passes on: Gain a Rare relic.
Result 2: He doesn't resist: Gain +1 Small Chest, but lose 1 Luck.
Result 3: Nothing.
What it is there: A cursed captain of Leoric's guard who asks the hero to find the Golden Elixir to lift his curse; his reward is the Veil of Steel.
Why it fits: A mercy-or-gain choice with a quest attached, which the event format holds in one screen.

Prompt: A huge pig lounges on a wooden dais, surrounded by obelisks. He looks at your pack with interest.
Result 1: Lose a food loot. The King is pleased: Gain +2 Gold.
Result 2: Lose a trinket. He tosses you something from his hoard: Gain a random loot.
Result 3: Nothing.
What it is there: Found in a Pig Village; he can't be harmed, and trades Gold Nuggets for meat and other offerings.
Why it fits: A trade for loot you don't need, which the food trinkets and the trinket pool give you plenty of.

Prompt: "Come closer, small one... Would you like to make a deal?!"
Result 1: Lose 3 Health. Usually: gain a random trinket. Rarely: gain a cursed relic instead.
Result 2: Lose 4 Max Health. Gain +1 Bash, Dash, Push, Transmute and Scramble.
Result 3: Usually nothing. Sometimes: "How dare you turn your back on me!" Gain a random curse.
What it is there: A goat demon offering deals that cost Health; leaving can bring Tragedy. The wiki notes it plays the role of Isaac's devil deal.
Why it fits: A deal with a price, and a price for refusing it. Isaac's devil deal is already in the inventory as items, never as an event.

Prompt: You come upon a strange mirror. Your reflection's movements are oddly delayed and distorted.
Result 1: Usually nothing. Sometimes you and your reflection swap places: gain a random Buff. If it goes wrong, you start your next game Terrified, or your reflection crawls out and stands on the board as an enemy.
Result 2: Usually: gain a loot from the glass. Sometimes: a Rare relic was hidden behind it. If it goes wrong: lose 2 Luck, or a curse.
Result 3: Nothing.
What it is there: A mirror event with intelligence- and strength-checked choices; its worst outcome spawns a copy of your cat as an enemy next fight.
Why it fits: Two gambles and a walk-away. The reflection stepping out onto the board is the memorable part.
Needs: new: a copy of the hero as an enemy

Prompt: The ghastly figure of Death appears. "I've seen you cheat death far too many times, and now I have come to reclaim what is rightfully mine... your soul!"
Result 1: Usually he spares you, amused. Sometimes he gives you a token: gain a trinket. If it goes wrong: Death stands up on the board as a boss.
Result 2: Usually he storms off. Sometimes you win his scythe: gain Death's Scythe. If it goes wrong: Death stands up on the board as a boss.
Result 3: You escape, for now. He will remember you.
What it is there: Appears to a cat with two or more Injuries. Charisma and intelligence checks can win a token or Death's own scythe, or start a fight with Death.
Why it fits: Fires when you are already hurting, which suits the Injury curse here, and its prize is a weapon candidate.

Prompt: "I got itchies and wheezies here for you!"
Result 1: Gain a cursed trinket, and a Flea fights beside you at the start of every game.
Result 2: Gain a random Debuff, and +2 Luck.
Result 3: "YOU WILL REGRET THAT!!!!" Gain a random curse.
What it is there: An NPC who makes you pick a parasite or a disease; refusing guarantees a Tragedy.
Why it fits: Every option costs something, and the choice is which cost; no live event is built that way.
Needs: new: an ally that joins every game

Prompt: You find a strange egg, larger than any you've seen. It appears to be quivering slightly.
Result 1: Usually: heal to full. Sometimes: Gain +1 Max Health. If it goes wrong: gain a Debuff, or a Mega Fetus stands up on the board.
Result 2: Usually: gain an egg trinket. Sometimes it hatches and follows you. If it goes wrong: a Mega Fetus stands up on the board.
Result 3: Nothing.
What it is there: A treasure-box event: smash it (strength) or loot it (dexterity), with outcomes from healing to an angry Mega Fetus.
Why it fits: A small, readable gamble with a body on the board as its downside, which the stack can carry.

Prompt: After the boss falls, a dark door opens. Inside, two items sit on pedestals, each priced in heart containers.
Result 1: Lose 1 Max Health. Gain a Boss relic.
Result 2: Lose 2 Max Health. Gain a Rare relic and a random Buff.
Result 3: Nothing. Your next Angel Room is more likely.
What it is there: May open after a boss is beaten; its items cost heart containers instead of coins. Sometimes Krampus waits inside instead.
Why it fits: The genre's most famous deal. Health-priced relics already exist (Calling Bell is a Boss relic); here they are a choice between games.

Requirement: no Devil Room deal taken this run
Prompt: A light-filled room. An angel statue watches over pedestals of free, holy items. Take one and the rest vanish.
Result 1: Gain a Rare relic of your choice of 2.
Result 2: Uriel or Gabriel steps out of it: a boss stands up on the board. Beat it for a Key Piece.
Result 3: Nothing.
What it is there: The divine counterpart of the Devil Room: free items (take one, the rest disappear); bombing the statue summons an angel.
Why it fits: The reward for refusing the Devil Room, which gives that event a cost beyond Health. Bombing the statue ties back to Mega Satan's key.
Needs: new: an event that remembers another event's choice

Prompt: You're ambushed crossing a rickety bridge over a river. The bandits demand a toll to cross.
Result 1: Lose 2 Gold (or, with less, your food loot).
Result 2: Two bandits stand up on the board.
Result 3: Needs Bash. Spend a Bash: they back off, and you cross for free.
What it is there: A common walking event: bandits demand food (or food, ammo and medicine) to cross; characters with the right traits get extra options.
Why it fits: Pay, fight or bluff: the classic toll, with a verb unlocking the third option the way a trait does there.

Prompt: The villagers here are not friendly. As punishment, they bring out... THE WHEEL. It spins...
Result 1: One of four: DINGUS DOO (nothing, but humiliating), HARD LABOR (lose 1 Health, gain +1 Max Health), GIFT BASKET (gain a random loot), DANG IT (lose a random loot).
Result 2: Spin again. Once only.
Result 3: Escape, but leave a random loot behind.
What it is there: A driving event: a village punishes the group with a wheel spin (DINGUS DOO, HARD LABOR, GIFT BASKET, DANG IT); a do-over can be demanded once, or the group can flee and lose the car.
Why it fits: A wheel is a gamble the player can see, and the one-time re-spin is a choice in itself.
Needs: new: a one-time re-roll inside an event

Prompt: An armed travelling chess master blocks the road. The game isn't optional, and if you lose, he takes his toll.
Result 1: A chance: win, and gain 2 Gold; lose, and lose 3 Gold or your food loot.
Result 2: If you have a familiar or a pet trinket, it eats the chess pieces. He's too stunned to collect: nothing lost.
Result 3: He stands up on the board as an enemy.
What it is there: A bandit event: a former chess champion forces a game; low-wits characters, animals and gourmands have their own ways out.
Why it fits: A forced gamble with a joke escape route, which is Death Road to Canada's humour in one screen.

Prompt: You are seized by a strange mood. You must build something, and nothing else matters, but you need materials.
Result 1: Lose 2 loot. You build an Artifact: gain a Rare relic.
Result 2: The mood turns. Lose 2 Health and gain a random Debuff.
What it is there: Dwarves periodically enter a strange mood, claim a workshop and demand materials for a legendary artifact; unable to finish, they go insane.
Why it fits: A trade of loot for a better relic, with a real cost for refusing. Dwarf Fortress's most famous story generator in one choice.
Builds on: lose loot, gain relic, random debuffs

Prompt: In a tent in the woods, a feathered fortune teller sits cross-legged among red candles. He lays two cards face up.
Result 1: Gain a random tarot card.
Result 2: Gain a random card.
Result 3: See a third card, and take one of the three.
What it is there: A resource NPC who runs a tarot shop in the woods: he deals two Tarot Cards and the Lamb picks one.
Why it fits: A pick-one-of-two for cards; the tarot family has 7 live pieces to draw from.

Prompt: Someone is caught in a giant spider web. A huge, fluffy spider is coming back for its meal.
Result 1: Lose 1 Health in the struggle. They thank you with a random loot.
Result 2: Pay 2 Gold. Gain +1 Max Health from the good deed.
Result 3: Helob eats well.
What it is there: A spider NPC who traps potential converts in webs and eats them if the Lamb doesn't save them (or buy them).
Why it fits: A rescue with a price, and a monster who is also a merchant.

Prompt: "Gamblers are tricksters, but they've a certain honor. Never to cheat and always to pay up when they lose."
Result 1: Four lucky rolls. 0 successes: lose all your Gold. 1-2: lose some Gold. 3: Gain +2 Gold. 4: double your Gold.
Result 2: Nothing.
What it is there: A random encounter that rolls 4 unfocusable luck slots for one of five outcomes, from losing all gold to doubling it.
Why it fits: A pure gamble with a graded result, which Luck here can steer; doubling Gold is already a card (2 of Diamonds).

Prompt: "Heated by volcanic vents, hot springs range from lukewarm to boiling hot."
Result 1: Three vitality rolls. 0 successes: lose 3 Health. 1: lose 1. 2: heal 1. 3: heal 3.
Result 2: Nothing.
What it is there: A random encounter that rolls 3 unfocusable vitality slots: from 40 damage to 40 healing.
Why it fits: A heal that can backfire, graded by how lucky you are; the healing verbs exist.

Prompt: "Some sort of power was nearly invoked here. If you can just make the correct adjustment you could unleash it for yourself."
Result 1: Four vitality rolls. 0: lose all but 1 Health. 1: an enemy stands up on the board. 2: a random curse. 3: Gain +1 Level. 4: Gain +1 Level and a Rare relic.
Result 2: Nothing, and it stays for later.
What it is there: A random encounter rolling 4 vitality slots: death, a fight, a random curse, experience, or a whole level.
Why it fits: Five rungs from disaster to jackpot, and every rung is something the game can already do.

Prompt: A rabbit in a black dress drops a prize into each of nine chests, then shuffles them. "You win some, you lose... a lot? Is that how it goes?"
Choice 1: Pay 2 Gold: open three of the nine chests
Result 1: Three random prizes: Gold, a potion, a relic, or a Pilfer that steals 1 Gold
Choice 2: Pay 1 Gold: pull one of three levers
Result 2: One does nothing, one destroys the chests, one opens them: Gain 2 Small Chests
Result 3: Nothing
What it is there: Black Rabbit hosts gambling rooms on runs: pay to pick three of nine shuffled chests (the prizes shown going in don't match what comes out), or pay to pull levers, one of which opens the chests.
Why it fits: A pay-to-gamble event with two games in one; the shell game's prizes are random whatever she shows, exactly as in hers.

Prompt: An orb hums in the first room of the floor.
Result 1: Drop to 1 Health. Beat the next 3 games and the peril lifts: Gain a random relic
Result 2: Nothing
What it is there: A curse taken from an orb in a floor's first room: it sets you to 1 HP and counts the rooms you must enter; at zero it lifts and gives a free relic.
Why it fits: A bet on yourself with a clock on it; nothing in the events asks you to play on at 1 Health.
Needs: new: a curse that pays out when it clears

Prompt: A bard sits on a blanket in a crawlspace, a tip bag at his feet.
Choice 1: Tip a tenth of your Gold (at least 1)
Result 1: Gain a random relic
Result 2: Choose one of 3 relics
Result 3: He complains
What it is there: A bard in secret rooms who asks for a tip: under 10% of your gold gets nothing, 10-49% a random relic, half or more a choice of 24 relics. Breaking his bag earns 1-3 curses.
Why it fits: A donation that scales with what you carry, so it's the same decision early and late in a run.

Prompt: An iron door, and behind it, treasure on altars, each in an open cage.
Result 1: Choose one of 3 pieces. The cages close on the other two
Result 2: Nothing
What it is there: Reward rooms behind an iron door whose key is elsewhere on the floor (a key holder: a secret room, a collapsing bridge, a guarded altar). Take one item from its cage and the others lock.
Why it fits: Nothing spends a key yet (inventory: keys); Brogue's vaults are what keys are for.

Prompt: Your attendants find a crown in the treasury that looks designed by an edgy jeweller. "Your Majesty! The Crown of Veldrath grants unmatched power... and, uh, mild insanity."
Result 1: 50%: Gain 2 Small Chests. 50%: nothing
Result 2: Gain +1 Strength for the rest of the run. You laugh at slightly inappropriate times
What it is there: An encounter: destroy the crown for a 50% chance at two building upgrades, give it to the madhouse for Madmen, or wear it for permanent morale.
Why it fits: A cursed item that turns out not to be: a gamble against a sure thing.

Prompt: The goblin army is scattered. Their emissary, an oddly polite fellow named Farto, offers a gift from their treasury in exchange for a truce.
Result 1: Gain +3 Gold
Result 2: Gain +1 Strength for the rest of the run. Their relatives come for revenge: 3 goblins stand up at the start of your next game
Result 3: Convince them you're a god: Gain a random weapon
What it is there: An encounter: accept the truce for metal, crush them for permanent morale and an immediate attack of 20 Goblin Pigs, or pose as a deity and get archers.
Why it fits: Three answers to one question, each a different reward, and the strong one comes with a fight.

Prompt: Your best battle mage, Redrum the Fiery, has entered the cooking contest. He holds out sausages and peas of a suspicious green. "My mother taught me this recipe, and my honour demands your honest opinion."
Result 1: You sip a healing potion between bites. Lose 1 Health, Gain 2 random potions
Choice 2: To serve such an awful dish deserves a beheading!
Result 2: Everyone works harder for a while: Gain +2 Gold
What it is there: An encounter: praise the dish (with a healing potion hidden in your wine) for two Healing Pool spells, behead Redrum for an Execution Ground, or fake a magical food allergy.
Why it fits: A food event that's about manners, not eating: the food family has nothing like it.

Prompt: Myrne has something bubbling. "Who's hungry?"
Result 1: Gain +1 Strength for the rest of the run. Lose 2 Health
Result 2: Nothing
What it is there: A run NPC whose every encounter is serving cooked food to one of your monsters: it gets stronger, and gains 7 Corruption (less Health at the start of every fight).
Why it fits: Getting stronger at the cost of health that doesn't come back easily: the same trade as hers, with Health standing in for Corruption.

Prompt: One of your men gets hit by birdshite.
Choice 1: "Yeah, don't dwell on it and let's get going."
Result 1: Lose 1 Luck
Result 2: Gain +1 Luck
Result 3: Gain a random food. Requires a weapon
What it is there: A daytime event: shrug it off (a bad mood, though a Historian cheers others), call it an omen with a Superstitious brother (good moods), or have a Hunter shoot the bird (good moods all round). A Lucky brother is never hit.
Why it fits: A pure flavour event with three tones; Luck stands in for mood.

Prompt: A small boy has climbed a tree to reach a ball stuck on the roof of his home. There's not a parent in sight.
Result 1: 70%: Gain +1 Luck. 30%: you fall off: Lose 1 Health
Result 2: Gain +1 Luck. Requires 1 Dash
Result 3: Nothing
What it is there: Help the boy (70% a reputation and a good mood, 30% the opposite), send a Sure Footing brother for a sure result, or walk on.
Why it fits: A small kindness with a chance of looking foolish, and a verb that makes it certain.

Prompt: A golden statue of a peglin, gleaming. Little bits of it look loose.
Choice 1: Spend all your Gold on it
Result 1: Gain a Rare weapon, all gold
Result 2: Lose Health equal to a third of your Gold. Gain 2 to 6 Gold
Result 3: Nothing
What it is there: Spend all your gold for the Ballectrum (a radiant golden orb), take damage worth 30% of your gold for a random pile of gold, or upgrade an orb cheaply. The gold option appears even if the damage would kill you.
Why it fits: Gold as health and health as gold, both ways round, with the greedy option able to kill you, as in the original.

Prompt: You stumble into a kitchen and are accosted by a peglin dressed up as a human chef. The humans haven't noticed. He'd like it to stay that way.
Result 1: Gain a random relic
Result 2: He bakes you The Cake: Gain +3 Max Health. Requires a food piece
What it is there: A Castle event: take the disguised chef's bribe for a relic; bring him the Egg and he bakes The Cake, a Portal reference that gives more max health than any other relic.
Why it fits: A food event with a secret recipe: the food family gets something to be traded for.

Prompt: Someone is calling for help from the next room: a damsel, a boyfriend, or a very nervous pug.
Result 1: Your next game carries the goal 'Get someone safely out of a level'. Meet it: Gain +1 Max Health
Result 2: Nothing
What it is there: Damsels (or a pug or boyfriend, by setting) call for help in the caves; carry one to the exit and you get a kiss and a heart. They can also be thrown, used as a shield, or sacrificed at Kali's altar.
Why it fits: An event that hands you a goal for the next game, with the classic Spelunky reward for meeting it.

Prompt: A gateway in the floor emblazoned with an eye opens and starts to smoke. A sacrifice is necessary to access the depths of Chaos.
Result 1: Chaos grants a boon with a catch: a random curse for 3 games, then, when it lifts, Gain a Rare item
Result 2: Nothing
What it is there: Chaos Gates cost Health to enter; inside, Chaos offers boons that curse you for a few encounters and then become a blessing for the rest of the run.
Why it fits: A boon that hurts first and pays later. Momentary Peril (candidate) sets you to 1 Health; this costs a little Health and a curse.
Needs: new: a curse that pays out when it clears

Prompt: Ragged folk fleeing the madness flag down your coach. They have little, and they need more.
Result 1: Lose 2 Gold. Remove a random Debuff
Result 2: Gain +3 Gold and a random Curse
Result 3: Nothing happens
What it is there: The Assistance Encounter: ordinary folk on the road, where each hero offers to Assist, Help, Inspire, Donate, Steal or Kill; helping is the main way to raise the Flame, the selfish choices pay more and lower it.
Why it fits: The good choice costs and the bad one pays, which is the encounter's whole point.
